ASAHI interviews Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro 🇵🇭 on the sidelines of the Shangri-La Dialogue: https://t.co/YWFvYWbk8q. He identifies Type-88 SSMs🇯🇵 as a serious candidate for acquisition & highlights Abukuma-class destroyers as a symbol of Tokyo's commitment to the region.

■Translation:

Philippine Defence Secretary Hopes for Japanese Arms Exports, Says Type 88 Anti-Ship Missile Is a “Strong Candidate”

Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro, speaking in an exclusive interview with The Asahi Shimbun in Singapore on 30 May, welcomed Japan’s recent revision of the implementation guidelines for its Three Principles on Transfer of Defence Equipment and Technology, which effectively lifted restrictions on arms exports. Regarding Japan’s Type 88 Surface-to-Ship Missile (SSM), designed to engage enemy vessels from land-based positions, Teodoro said it was “one of the strong candidates” for acquisition.

The Type 88 SSM is the missile system that the Japan Self-Defense Forces used in a live-fire exercise during Balikatan, the large-scale U.S.-Philippine military exercise held in the Philippines in April and May this year. While noting that there are other systems with comparable capabilities and that Manila would determine the most suitable option, Teodoro said that the Type 88 SSM was “a candidate we are seriously considering.” He added that he had discussed the system’s performance and potential deployment locations with Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi.

Japan and the Philippines have also agreed to begin consultations on the possible transfer of the JMSDF’s Abukuma-class destroyer escorts. Teodoro emphasised the significance of such a transfer, stating that it would “symbolise Japan’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific.” He added that “active discussions are taking place with the Japanese government regarding defence industrial cooperation.”
